extracted.intended_audience: lawmakers, state officials, lawyers, corporations, and citizens of Oklahoma
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted provisions from the Oklahoma Constitution covering arbitration, state seal, jury procedure, corporate and public-utility regulation, revenue and taxation, homestead protections, municipal organization, and initiative/referendum rules. The page lists statutory requirements, powers, prohibitions, procedural rules, and provisos applicable within the State of Oklahoma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 154 — Board of Arbitration and Conciliation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Legislature shall create a Board of Arbitration and Conciliation in the Department of Labor and the Commissioner of Labor shall be ex-officio chairman.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 168 — Seal of the State
rubrics_metrics.description: The center shall be a five pointed star...the center of the star shall contain the central device of the seal of the Territory of Oklahoma, including the words 'Labor Omnia Vincit.' Each ray shall contain specified symbols of the Cherokee, Chickasaw, Creek, Choctaw, and Seminole Nations; forty-five small stars grouped between rays represent the forty-five states then in the Union; a circular band shall be inscribed 'Great Seal of the State of Oklahoma, 1907.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies detailed heraldic imagery and inscriptions for the official state seal; includes arrangement, symbolism, and inscription text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 193 — Trial by Jury Waived
rubrics_metrics.description: In all issues of fact joined in any court, all parties may waive the right to have the same determined by jury; in which case the finding of the judge, upon the facts, shall have the force and effect of a verdict by jury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 194 — Jury to Return General Verdict; Court May Direct Special Findings
rubrics_metrics.description: In all jury trials, the jury shall return a general verdict, and no law shall require the court to direct the jury to make findings on particular questions of fact; but the court may, in its discretion, direct such special findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 205 — Definition of 'Corporation' and 'Charter' and 'License'
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'corporation' or 'company' includes all associations and joint stock companies having any power or privileges not possessed by individuals, and excludes municipal corporations and public institutions owned/controlled by the State; 'charter' means the charter of incorporation; 'license' means authority permitting foreign corporations to transact business in the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 206 — Common Carriers; Right to Construct and Operate Lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Every railroad, oil pipe, car, express, telephone or telegraph corporation organized or authorized to do a transportation or transmission business in this State shall have the right to construct and operate its line between any points in this State and connect at the State line with like lines; each shall have the right to intersect, connect with, or cross any railroad or such line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants construction/operation and interconnection rights to specified transportation/transmission corporations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 207 — To Transport Each Other's Cars and Passengers
rubrics_metrics.description: Every railroad, car, or express company shall receive and transport without delay or discrimination each other's cars, loaded or empty, tonnage, and passengers, under such rules and regulations as may be prescribed by law or any commission created by the Constitution or by act of the Legislature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes non-discriminatory interchange and reciprocal carriage duties; subject to regulatory rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 208 — Oil Pipe Companies Subject to Control of Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: All oil pipe companies shall be subject to the reasonable control and regulation of the Corporation Commission, and shall receive and transport each other's tonnage, oils, or commodities under rules and regulations prescribed by law or such commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Places oil pipeline carriers under Corporation Commission jurisdiction for reasonable control and regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 209 — Telephone and Telegraph Lines to Transmit Each Other's Messages
rubrics_metrics.description: All telephone and telegraph lines operated for hire shall receive and transmit each other's messages without delay or discrimination, and make physical connections with each other's lines, under rules and regulations prescribed by law or commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates interoperability and nondiscrimination among commercial communications lines, subject to regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 210 — Railroads Public Highways; Office in State; Meetings and Reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Railroads are declared public highways. Every railroad or other public service corporation doing business in this State shall maintain a public office or place in this State for business transactions, keep records for inspection by stockholders (capital subscribed, owners, transfers, assets/liabilities, officers), hold at least one meeting annually in the State with thirty days' public notice, and the president/superintendent shall report annually under oath and make other reports as required by law or Corporation Commission; Legislature shall enforce provisions with penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires in-state office, recordkeeping, annual in-state director meeting, sworn annual reporting to the Corporation Commission, and enforcement by legislation/penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 211 — Rolling Stock Considered Personal Property, Subject to Sale
rubrics_metrics.description: Rolling stock and all other movable property of railroads or other public corporations shall be considered personal property and liable to execution and sale like property of individuals; Legislature shall pass no laws exempting such property from execution and sale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 212 — Must Not Consolidate with Competing Lines
rubrics_metrics.description: No public service corporation or its lessees/purchasers/managers shall consolidate stock, property, or franchises with or control any other public service corporation owning a parallel or competing line, nor shall officers act as officers of competing corporations, except by enactment of Legislature upon recommendation of the Corporation Commission; Legislature shall never permit foreign (other-state or U.S.) public service corporations to consolidate with other such corporations owning parallel lines in this State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits consolidation/dual-office holding among competing public service corporations, with narrow legislative exception and strict ban on foreign corporate consolidations controlling parallel lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 213 — Must Not Consolidate with Company Organized in Another State
rubrics_metrics.description: No railroad, transportation, or transmission company organized under the laws of this State shall consolidate by private or judicial sale or otherwise with any company organized under the laws of any other State or of the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 214 — Street Railroad; Consent of Local Authorities Required
rubrics_metrics.description: No law shall be passed granting the right to construct and operate a street railroad within any city, town, or village, or upon any public highway, without first acquiring the consent of the local authorities having control of the street or highway proposed to be occupied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 215 — Must Accept Provisions of Constitution
rubrics_metrics.description: No public service corporation in existence at adoption of this Constitution shall have the benefit of future legislation except upon condition of complete acceptance of all provisions of this Constitution applicable to such corporations; nothing shall validate any invalid charter or waive charter conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions future legislative benefits on corporations' acceptance of constitutional provisions; preserves challenges to invalid charters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 216 — No Railroad to Transport Articles Manufactured by It
rubrics_metrics.description: No railroad company shall transport within this State any article or commodity manufactured, mined, or produced by it or in which it has any interest, except articles necessary and intended for its use in the conduct of its business as a common carrier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits common carriers from self-dealing by transporting their own manufactured/owned goods for general commercial purposes, with limited exception for carrier's business needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 217 — No Free Transportation; Exceptions; Penalty for Violation
rubrics_metrics.description: No railroad, transportation, or transmission company shall issue or give free franks, tickets, passes or other free transportation within this State except to enumerated categories (employees and families, officers, agents, surgeons, physicians, attorneys, ministers, certain charity recipients, indigent persons transported by charitable societies, veterans' home inmates, volunteer fire dept. members while traveling as such, necessary caretakers of livestock/fruit, employees of sleeping/express cars, linemen, Railway Mail Service employees, inspectors, newsboys on trains, baggage agents, witnesses in legal investigations in which company is interested, persons injured in wrecks, attending physicians/nurses). Interchange of passes among carriers' officers/employees and free transport to provide relief in epidemics/pestilence/calamity and for transporting persons entering service to employment are allowed. Any other grant/use of such free transportation is a crime; Legislature shall provide penalties and may extend exceptions by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive exception list and provisos; creates criminal prohibition for unauthorized free transportation and delegates penalty-setting to Legislature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 218 — Railroads to Pass Through County Seats
rubrics_metrics.description: No railroad hereafter constructed in this State shall pass within four miles of any county seat without passing through it and establishing/maintaining a depot therein, unless prevented by natural obstacles; provided such town or citizens grant right-of-way and sufficient ground for depot purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions routing obligations on construction of new railroads to serve county seats and requires local cooperation for right-of-way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 219 — Corporation Commission: Election, Terms, Vacancy
rubrics_metrics.description: A Corporation Commission of three persons is created, to be elected by the people at a general election for State officers for six-year terms; first commissioners' terms are staggered; in case of vacancy, the Governor appoints until next general election when successor is elected to fill unexpired term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes composition, term length, initial staggering, and gubernatorial appointment process for vacancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 231 — Appeals to Supreme Court; Acts of Commission Not to be Suspended Except by Supreme Court
rubrics_metrics.description: From any action of the Commission prescribing rates, charges, classifications of traffic, affecting train schedule, requiring additional facilities/conveniences/public service, refusing to approve/suspending bond or requiring additional security, an appeal (subject to reasonable limits as to time, procedure, cost prescribed by law) may be taken by the corporation affected or any aggrieved person or State (if allowed by law). Until otherwise provided, such appeal shall be taken in the manner appeals are taken to the Supreme Court from District Courts, except that such an appeal shall be of right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits direct appeals of Corporation Commission actions to the Supreme Court as of right, subject to legislatively prescribed procedural limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 242 — Commission to Ascertain Cost, Indebtedness, Bonds, and Salaries; Annual Report
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission shall ascertain and record as public record (as early as practicable) amounts expended in construction and equipment per mile of every railroad and public service corporation, costs to procure right of way, costs to reconstruct physical properties, outstanding bonds/debentures/indebtedness (amounts, when issued, interest rate, purposes, use of proceeds, to whom issued/sold and price), what became of the proceeds, by whom indebtedness held and amounts due, floating indebtedness and creditors' addresses, credits due, property on hand, judicial/other sales and amounts paid and how paid, and amounts paid for officers' salaries and employees' wages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates comprehensive financial and property disclosure by public service corporations to the Corporation Commission for public record and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 245 — Duty of Commission to Investigate Rates; May Make Corrections and Notify Interstate Commerce Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission must investigate all through freight or passenger rates on railroads in the State and, when rates are excessive or violate the Interstate Commerce Law or ICC rules/regulations, notify proper railroad officials to reduce or correct them; if not changed, the Commission must notify the ICC and apply for relief and the Attorney General or designated persons shall represent the Commission in such matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires proactive rate oversight, corrective requests, and escalation to federal Interstate Commerce Commission if state-level corrections are not made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 251 — Two Cents Per Mile Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: No person/company/corporation operating a railroad (other than street/electric railroad) shall demand or receive for first-class transportation per passenger between points within this State more than two cents per mile until otherwise provided by law; provided the Corporation Commission may exempt any railroad upon satisfactory proof that it cannot earn just compensation if limited to two cents per mile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets a maximum statutory passenger fare subject to Commission exemptions for financial hardship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 254 — Must Not Contribute to Elections
rubrics_metrics.description: No corporation organized or doing business in this State shall be permitted to influence elections or official duty by contributions of money or anything of value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits corporate contributions to influence elections or official duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 255 — Shall Not Own Stock of Another Corporation
rubrics_metrics.description: No corporation chartered or licensed to do business in this State shall own, hold, or control the stock of any competitive corporation engaged in the same kind of business in or out of the State, except stock pledged in good faith to secure bona fide indebtedness acquired upon foreclosure, execution, sale, or otherwise for satisfaction of debt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents cross-ownership among competing corporations, with narrow pledge exception for debt security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 256 — Must Dispose of Stock in Twelve Months; Bank and Trust Company Restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: When any corporation acquires stock in another corporation as provided, it must dispose of it within twelve months and during ownership may not participate in control except by Corporation Commission order; no trust company or bank shall own/hold/control stock of another trust/bank except stock pledged in good faith to secure bona fide indebtedness, and such stock must be disposed of in the time and manner provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires prompt divestiture of acquired competitive stock and imposes restrictions on bank/trust company cross-ownership, subject to Commission order in limited cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 257 — Must Submit to Arbitration
rubrics_metrics.description: Every license issued or charter granted to a mining or public service corporation, foreign or domestic, shall contain a stipulation that such corporation will submit any difference it may have with employees in reference to labor to arbitration as provided by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates arbitration clauses in charters/licenses for labor disputes; jurisdiction to be provided by law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 260 — Monopoly; Must Not Discriminate
rubrics_metrics.description: Until otherwise provided by law, no person, firm, association, or corporation engaged in production, manufacture, distribution, or sale of any commodity of general use shall, for the purpose of creating a monopoly or destroying competition, discriminate between different persons/associations/corporations or different sections/communities/cities by selling such commodity at a lower rate in one section than another after allowance for differences in grade, quantity, quality, and actual cost of transportation from point of production/manufacture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits discriminatory pricing intended to create monopoly or destroy competition; requires consideration of legitimate cost/quality/transportation differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 271 — Exemptions; Manufacturing Establishments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Legislature may authorize any incorporated city or town, by majority vote of its electors voting thereon, to exempt manufacturing establishments and public utilities from municipal taxation for a period not exceeding five years as inducement to location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows temporary municipal tax exemptions as economic incentives, subject to local voter approval and five-year cap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 272 — Assessments for Local Improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Legislature may authorize county and municipal corporations to levy and collect assessments for local improvements upon property benefited thereby, homesteads included, without regard to a cash valuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits special assessments on benefited property including homesteads; valuation method not limited to cash valuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 273 — Property Assessed at Fair Cash Value; Penalty
rubrics_metrics.description: All property taxable ad valorem shall be assessed at its fair cash value, estimated at the price it would bring at a fair voluntary sale; any officer or person authorized to assess values who commits malfeasance shall, upon conviction, forfeit office and be otherwise punished as by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates fair cash value assessment standard and penalizes malfeasant assessors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 281 — Credit of State Not Given
rubrics_metrics.description: The credit of the State shall not be given, pledged, or loaned to any individual, company, corporation, association, municipality, or political subdivision; nor shall the State become an owner or stockholder in, nor make donation by gift or subscription to stock, by tax or otherwise, to any company, association, or corporation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits State credit pledging, ownership, or gifts/subscriptions to private entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 289 — State May Contract Debts; Limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The State may, to meet casual deficits or failure in revenues, or for expenses not provided for, contract debts; but such debts direct and contingent shall not at any time exceed four hundred thousand dollars, and moneys from loans must be applied to the purpose obtained or to repay debts and to no other purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits limited temporary borrowing with a strict statewide cap and purpose limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 290 — May Contract Debts to Repel Invasion
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to the above limited power to contract debts, the State may contract debts to repel invasion, suppress insurrection or to defend the State in war; money from such debts shall be applied to the purpose raised or to repay such debts and to no other purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows borrowing beyond ordinary cap for defense/emergency purposes with strict application limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 291 — Debts; Limitations; Submitted to People
rubrics_metrics.description: Except debts specified in sections 23 and 24 of this article, no debts shall be contracted by or on behalf of the State unless authorized by law for some work or object distinctly specified therein; such law shall impose/ provide collection of a direct annual tax sufficient to pay interest as it falls due and discharge principal within twenty-five years; no such law takes effect until submitted at a general election and receives majority of votes cast for and against it; on final passage question shall be put 'Shall this bill pass, and ought the same to receive the sanction of the people?' with yeas and nays entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires voter approval for most State debts, statutory specificity of purpose, tax provision for repayment, and legislative recordkeeping (yeas and nays).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 292 — Limitation Upon Debts of City, County, etc.; Vote by People; Sinking Fund
rubrics_metrics.description: No county, city, town, township, school district, or other political corporation/subdivision shall become indebted in any manner for any purpose exceeding the income/revenue for that year without assent of three-fifths of voters voting at an election; and in cases requiring such assent, total indebtedness including existing shall not exceed five percent of valuation of taxable property ascertained from last assessment; such political corporations incurring indebtedness requiring voter assent shall before or at the time provide for collection of an annual tax sufficient to pay interest as it falls due and to constitute a sinking fund to pay principal within twenty-five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets voter-approval thresholds, aggregate indebtedness limits tied to property valuation, and sinking-fund/tax collection requirements for local government debt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 293 — Public Utilities; Indebtedness for; Sinking Fund
rubrics_metrics.description: An incorporated city or town may, by majority of qualified property tax paying voters voting at election, be allowed to become indebted in larger amount than specified for the purpose of purchasing or constructing public utilities or repairing same to be owned exclusively by such city; any such city incurring such indebtedness must provide for collection of an annual tax in addition to other taxes sufficient to pay interest as it falls due and to constitute a sinking fund for payment of principal within twenty-five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits voter-approved extra indebtedness for municipal utilities with required supplementary tax and sinking-fund arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 304 — Homestead: What to Consist Of
rubrics_metrics.description: The homestead of any family not within a city/town/village shall consist of not more than 160 acres (one or more parcels) selected by the owner; homestead within city/town/village owned/occupied as residence only shall consist of not exceeding one acre selected by owner provided the same shall not exceed in value $5,000 and in no event shall homestead be reduced to less than one-quarter of an acre without regard to value; if used for both residence and business, homestead interest shall not exceed in value $5,000; nothing in U.S. laws or treaties with Indian Tribes shall deprive any Indian/allottee of homestead/exemption laws benefit; temporary renting of the homestead shall not change its character when no other homestead acquired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines rural and urban homestead acreage and value limits, protections for Indian allottees, and preserves homestead character through temporary renting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 305 — Homestead: Protected from Forced Sale; Consent of Spouse
rubrics_metrics.description: The homestead shall be protected from forced sale for payment of debts except for purchase money, taxes due, or for work and material used in constructing improvements; owner if married shall not sell homestead without spouse's consent given as prescribed by law; nothing prevents mortgaging homestead with spouse joining or sale on foreclosure to satisfy such mortgage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides strong protection against forced sale with specified exceptions and requires spousal consent for sale; allows mortgage transactions with spouse's joiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 316 — Legal Rate of Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The legal rate of interest shall not exceed six percent per annum in absence of contract; by contract parties may agree upon any rate not to exceed ten percent per annum; until reduced by Legislature, six percent and ten percent are respectively the legal and maximum contract rates of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets default and maximum contract interest rates and reserves legislative power to change them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 411 — Legislature May Provide for Organization (Municipal Corporations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Municipal corporations shall not be created by special laws; the Legislature by general laws shall provide for incorporation and organization of cities and towns and classification in proportion to population subject to the provisions of this article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires uniform general laws for municipal creation/organization and classification by population; forbids special laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 413 — Procedure for Obtaining Special Charter; Election; Ratification; Governor Approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Any city with population >2,000 may frame its own charter by electing a board of freeholders (two from each ward qualified electors) to prepare and propose a charter within 90 days; charter to be signed in duplicate, one copy to chief executive officer and other to Register of Deeds; proposed charter published in local newspapers for specified periods and then submitted to electors within 30 days (not earlier than 20) after publication; if majority ratifies, submit to Governor who shall approve if not in conflict with Constitution and laws; upon approval it becomes organic law superseding existing charters/ordinances inconsistent with it; certified copies deposited with Secretary of State and city archives; courts shall take judicial notice; charter amendments may be proposed by legislative authority or petition and ratified by majority and approved by Governor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies detailed procedural steps, publication timing, electoral ratification, gubernatorial approval, recordation, and amendment process for special city charters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 414 — Board of Freeholders to Draft Charter; Election Call by Petition
rubrics_metrics.description: An election for board of freeholders may be called by legislative authority and must be called by chief executive officer within ten days after filing of a petition signed by qualified electors equal to 25% of votes cast at preceding general municipal election; election held within 30 days after call; at such election vote on whether to proceed; unless majority favor proceeding no further proceedings shall be had and prior proceedings are of no effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives citizens the mechanism (petition threshold and timelines) to demand charter-drafting board and requires majority support to proceed further.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 415 — Initiative and Referendum Reserved to Every Municipality
rubrics_metrics.description: The powers of initiative and referendum reserved by this Constitution to the people of the State and the respective counties/districts are reserved to the people of every municipal corporation now existing or created within the State with reference to all legislative authority it may exercise and amendments to charters for its own government in accordance with Constitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures municipal-level initiative/referendum powers consistent with state constitutional reservations and charter amendment processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 416 — Petition for Initiative/Referendum; Requisite Number
rubrics_metrics.description: Every petition for either the initiative or referendum in the government of a municipal corporation shall be signed by a number of qualified electors residing within the municipality (text cut off in chunk).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that initiative/referendum petitions must meet a signature threshold of qualified local electors; full numeric threshold and detailed procedural rules appear beyond the chunk.
